public_claim: NASA reports the experimental X-59 reached supersonic speed in 2026 and is being flown to validate quiet-supersonic research and later gather community-response data.
certification_state: research flight testing; not a passenger-airliner certification record
what_it_supports: an active public research path for noise and flight evidence
what_it_does_not_support: commercial passenger service, passenger economics, or a current practical-airliner pass

public_claim: FAA granted a special authorization for supersonic testing of the XB-1 experimental aircraft and explicitly states that the authorization does not establish airworthiness or other certification requirements.
certification_state: limited test authorization only; no passenger certification
what_it_supports: a primary-source distinction between authorized research testing and commercial approval
what_it_does_not_support: passenger service, transport-category certification, or proof that Overture is ready

public_claim: Boom reports that the XB-1 demonstrator is intended to inform development of the Overture airliner and describes future commercial passenger ambitions.
certification_state: company programme claim; no independent passenger-service or certification record in this close read
what_it_supports: that a live private-sector programme exists and has reached a flying demonstrator milestone
what_it_does_not_support: a certified passenger aircraft, delivered service, or independently verified practicality

public_claim: FAA describes an initial proposed rule and a future noise-threshold rule as steps toward commercial supersonic flight; the page says the pathway is still being established.
certification_state: proposed and future rulemaking; not a final commercial authorization
what_it_supports: why regulatory progress is a prerequisite evidence category
what_it_does_not_support: a final rule, aircraft certification, community acceptance, or passenger service
